structure.title: Study Hours vs. GMAT Score Improvement Over 12 Weeks

question: Based on the line chart, the study hours per week peaked at week _____, while the GMAT score improvement showed diminishing returns after week _____, indicating that additional study hours beyond that point yielded progressively smaller gains.
title: MBA Study Hours vs. GMAT Score Improvement: Peak and Diminishing Returns
solution:
Step 1: Identify the peak of study hours per week from the line chart.
The study hours line shows values: week 1: 10, week 2: 12, week 3: 15, week 4: 18, week 5: 20, week 6: 22, week 7: 25, week 8: 28, week 9: 25, week 10: 22, week 11: 20, week 12: 18.
The highest value is 28 hours at week 8.
Step 2: Determine when GMAT score improvement shows diminishing returns.
Diminishing returns means each additional unit of input (study hours) yields progressively smaller gains in output (score improvement).
Calculate the incremental improvement per week: week 1 to 2: 5 points, week 2 to 3: 10 points, week 3 to 4: 15 points, week 4 to 5: 15 points, week 5 to 6: 15 points, week 6 to 7: 15 points, week 7 to 8: 10 points, week 8 to 9: 5 points, week 9 to 10: 3 points, week 10 to 11: 2 points, week 11 to 12: 2 points.
The increments start decreasing after week 8 (from 15 to 10), with a more pronounced drop after week 8.
Step 3: Interpret the business context.
In MBA preparation, diminishing returns suggest optimal study strategy; after week 8, additional hours yield minimal score gains, indicating a potential saturation point.
Step 4: Verify with the graph.
The study hours peak at week 8, and the GMAT improvement curve flattens noticeably after week 8, confirming diminishing returns.
Step 5: Conclude the answers.
First blank: 8 (peak study hours).
Second blank: 8 (start of diminishing returns in score improvement).
